instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in the conversation between these two Georgian women.

hint.label: Georgian
hint.text: The Georgian era was named after King George I, II, III and IV, who ruled Britain from 1714 to 1830.
hint.sound: The Georgian era was named after King George I, second, third and fourth, who ruled Britain from 1714 to 1830.

atoms.b: Have you heard about the ((++smallpox starburst)) outbreak?
Yes, people are falling ill in the ((++city sky)). I was there just last week.
Isn’t it strange that we haven’t ((++caught chased)) smallpox yet?
Well, we did already get ((++cowpox malaria)) from our cows, and that’s quite similar. Maybe that’s why?

feedback.finish: She’s right! Many milkmaids were immune to smallpox because they had already had cowpox — a similar, but milder, disease.

feedback.end: This man is Edward Jenner, the scientist who noticed milkmaids’ immunity to smallpox. He used this to create the first vaccine in 1796.

atoms.sound: Vaccines are weak versions of an illness.

atoms.a: They are injected into our bodies, and ...
atoms.b: our immune system can easily kill them.
atoms.sound: They are injected into our bodies, and our immune system can easily kill them.

atoms.a: This gives our bodies practice and stops us from ...
atoms.b: getting the illness more seriously in the future.
atoms.sound: This gives our bodies practice and stops us from getting the illness more seriously in the future.

instruction.text: Vaccines were not the only important medical invention of the time. Match each Georgian and Victorian medical invention to its name.

feedback.correct: X-rays were invented in 1895 and help doctors to see broken bones.
Stethoscopes are used to listen to people’s heartbeats. They were invented in 1816.
Antiseptics are things that kill germs. The first antiseptic was invented by Joseph Lister in 1867.
